name: Chart of accounts and journal entries
Bank reconciliation with a matching widget
note: Community reconciles manually. The community widget covers the same ground as the Enterprise one, and it is the module our clients notice first.

name: Bank statement import in OFX and CAMT
Financial statements and trial balance
note: Community ships generic reports. The community set adds the aged balances, the general ledger with a drill-down and a report builder.

name: Deferred revenue and expense
note: The accrual entries are covered, the Enterprise deferral wizard is not. Usually handled with a recurring entry template.

name: Multi-currency with automatic rates
note: Community handles multi-currency. The community module fetches the daily rate from the Brazilian central bank.

name: Multi-company consolidation
note: An honest gap. Consolidation is usually done outside the ERP or through a report builder.

name: NF-e issuing and receiving
note: The community localisation issues the document natively. The Enterprise localisation relies on a paid third-party tax service.

name: NFS-e for services
note: Coverage depends on the municipality. The national standard is supported; some city systems still need a dedicated adapter. This is the row we get asked about most, and the one where a vague answer costs a project.

name: Brazilian tax calculation engine
note: The tax model is generic by design, which is why new taxes enter as new records instead of as a rewrite of the engine.

name: SPED Fiscal and Contribuicoes
note: Partial by design: most clients generate the files from the accounting data and validate them in a specialist tool.

name: ECD and ECF accounting bookkeeping
note: Delivered together with the client accounting firm rather than fully inside the ERP.

name: Pix collection and reconciliation
note: Delivered per bank on top of the payment order framework. There is no single generic module yet, and we say so.

name: Fiscal document storage and XML archive
IBS and CBS tax reform readiness
note: Being built upstream, in the open, for a transition that runs to 2033. It lands on the current versions first, which is what turns an old version into an upgrade decision.

name: Order types with their own defaults
note: A community module with no Enterprise equivalent, and one of the most requested in Brazil.

name: Recurring contracts and subscriptions
note: The community contract module is what our service clients run, recurring invoicing included.

name: Business rule blocks on order confirmation
Online appointment booking
note: An honest gap: Enterprise only, with no community equivalent we would recommend.

name: Internal purchase requests
note: Enterprise covers this in a separate Approvals app. The community module lives inside purchasing, where the buyer actually works.

name: Calls for tender and supplier comparison
Supplier price lists and lead times
Three-way match on supplier invoices
note: Standard behaviour in both editions through the bill control policy on received quantities.

name: Business rule blocks on purchase confirmation
Available to promise and release strategies
Block negative stock
note: Standard Odoo allows negative stock in both editions. This is one of the first modules we install on a distribution project.

name: Make to order and make to stock per line
Carrier integration and shipping labels
note: The framework is shared. Brazilian carrier adapters are usually built per client, and we say so before the project starts.

name: Packaging and unit of measure conversion
Advanced warehouse routing and zone picking
note: The community warehouse suite goes further than Enterprise here.

name: Bills of material with variants and phantoms
Multi-level material planning
note: Enterprise calls it the master production schedule. The community module plans the full bill of material tree, and it is what we deploy.

name: Shop floor tablet interface
note: An honest gap. The Enterprise shop floor screen has no equivalent; we deliver a simplified kiosk view instead.

name: Engineering change orders
note: An honest gap: the Enterprise product lifecycle app is not matched by a community module.

name: Internal audits and ISO management system
note: A whole management system suite with no Enterprise counterpart.

name: Spare parts consumption on work orders
Availability and reliability indicators
note: Mean time between failures and mean time to repair are built per client on the maintenance records. There is no generic module we would recommend.

name: Field service orders and scheduling
note: The community field service suite is the most complete in the ecosystem and stands comparison with the Enterprise app.

name: Routes and day planning per technician
Van stock and parts consumed in the field
Offline mobile app for technicians
note: An honest gap. The Enterprise mobile app works offline; a community deployment uses a responsive web view, which needs connectivity.

name: Repair orders with parts and labour
Repair types with their own workflow
Return merchandise authorisation
note: The community RMA suite is the reference implementation. Neither edition ships a dedicated RMA app.

name: Warranty control on repairs
note: Delivered on top of the repair type and the equipment history rather than by a single module.

name: Service history by serial number
note: Assembled from the standard serial traceability report rather than from a dedicated module, so it answers what happened to a unit without giving you a per-unit service file.

name: Capacity forecast and resource planning
note: Enterprise has a dedicated planning app. The community module covers the forecast without the drag and drop board.

name: Time off and public holidays
note: The community module loads the Brazilian national, state and municipal holiday calendars.

name: Appraisals and skill management
note: An honest gap: the Enterprise appraisal app is not matched by a community module.

name: Brazilian payroll
note: Neither edition solves Brazilian payroll. We integrate a specialist payroll provider and post the accounting entries. Anyone telling you otherwise has not run a Brazilian payroll.

name: eSocial and labour filings
note: Same as payroll: delivered by the specialist provider and integrated into the accounting.

name: Marketing automation workflows
note: An honest gap: Enterprise only.

name: Helpdesk and support tickets
note: The community helpdesk is what we run ourselves and for our support clients.

name: Social media publishing
note: An honest gap: Enterprise only.

name: Live spreadsheet reports
note: An honest gap. The Enterprise spreadsheet is genuinely good. The community answer is a report builder plus exports.

name: Pivot and graph views on any model
Custom SQL views exposed as reports
Export to an external business intelligence tool
note: Read-only database access is available in both editions when you host it yourself, and not on the vendor cloud.

name: No-code customisation studio
note: An honest gap, and one of the real reasons to choose Enterprise. We reach the same result in code, versioned and reviewable, but it is not a drag and drop screen.

name: Customisation through versioned modules
note: The same mechanism in both editions. On Community you also own the deployment, which is what makes the code portable.

name: REST API with a documented schema
note: Standard Odoo exposes remote procedure calls. The community framework adds a documented REST layer, in either edition.

name: Asynchronous job queue
note: No Enterprise equivalent, and any serious integration needs it.

name: Integration framework with mapping and retries
Document management with folders and rights
Electronic signature
note: The community module signs documents. It does not have the Enterprise template gallery.

name: Industrial device and scale integration
note: An honest gap. Devices are integrated case by case over the network rather than through a dedicated box.

name: Telephony integration
note: An honest gap: integrated per telephone system when a client needs it.

name: Branded native mobile app
note: An honest gap, and a real reason to choose Enterprise. The community answer is a responsive web interface.

name: Users, groups and record level rules
Audit trail of data changes
note: Neither Odoo edition ships an audit log. This is the row auditors ask about, and the community is the one that answers it.

name: Generic multi-level approval on any document
Consent register and data subject requests
note: What a Brazilian data protection audit asks for, answered by a community module in either edition.

name: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect or SAML
Choice of data residency and hosting provider
note: Self-hosting is possible in both editions, but the vendor cloud fixes the region for you. This is the row that decides public sector and regulated deals.

name: Full source code access
note: Community is licensed as free software. Enterprise source is available under a subscription agreement that ends when the subscription does.

name: Leaving the supplier without losing the system
note: On Community the repository and the deployment recipe are yours. Changing supplier becomes a commercial decision instead of a technical drama.
